title: What Kind of Lover Are You?

chapters.title: How you fall
chapters.teaser: Fast, slow, sideways or all at once. The way your soul actually falls for someone.

chapters.title: Your flirting style
chapters.teaser: What you think you're doing, what they think you're doing, and the one move that lands.

chapters.title: Your attachment pattern
chapters.teaser: Clingy, cool, steady or somewhere in between. How you hold on when you care.

chapters.title: Jealousy and your trigger
chapters.teaser: The exact thing that sets you off, and what you do instead of saying it.

chapters.title: Yeon's red flag report
chapters.teaser: The love habit you keep repeating. Yeon does not soften this chapter.

chapters.title: What you actually need
chapters.teaser: Not your type. Your match. The kind of person and love that lets you relax.

text.how-you-fall: You don't fall, you decide. Somewhere around the third conversation you look at a person and think, yes, this one is worth building something with, and from then on you are all in. Gap is the tall tree, and trees don't wander off to see what else is growing. The catch is that your decision often comes before the other person has made theirs. You can mistake your own certainty for proof that it's mutual. You also fall for potential. You see who someone could become in five years and you love that version a little too early. When it works, it's beautiful: steady, loyal, protective love that makes people feel chosen. When it doesn't, you stay far longer than the evidence allows, because leaving feels like admitting you planted in the wrong field.
text.flirting: Your flirting looks a lot like mentoring. You ask about their plans, you give advice nobody requested, you show up with a solution to the problem they mentioned last Tuesday. To you, this is romance. To them, it can feel like a very attractive performance review. You are not a giggler or a hair-twirler. You flirt with competence and reliability, and the people who get it find it irresistible. The people who don't think you're just being nice. Try this: say one thing you like about them that has nothing to do with their potential. Not "you'd be great at this job." Something like "I like how you laugh at your own jokes before the punchline." Small, specific, a little soft. It lands harder than any plan you could make for them.
text.attachment: Your pattern sits close to what psychologists would call secure on the surface, with a hidden streak of control underneath. You are steady. You text back. You keep promises. But you also want things to grow in a direction you can see, and when a partner drifts or goes quiet, you don't panic, you start managing. You suggest, you organize, you quietly take over. It feels like care. It can land as pressure. The tree wants to be the thing everyone leans on, and being leaned on feels safer than leaning. The honest question for you is not "do I love well?" You do. It's "can I let someone else hold the plan for a while without checking on it?" That's where your next level of closeness lives.
text.jealousy: You don't do loud jealousy. You do principled jealousy. You won't check their phone, because that's beneath you, but you will notice that they replied to someone else's story in four minutes and yours in four hours, and you will file it away. Your trigger is disrespect more than competition. You can handle a partner having attractive friends. What you can't handle is feeling like you were an option rather than the choice. When it hits, you go stiff and formal, which confuses people, because you seem fine and you are absolutely not fine. The fix is boring and it works: say it early, in one plain sentence. "That made me feel like a backup." You're good at direct. Use it on your own feelings, not just everyone else's problems.
text.red-flag: Yeon's verdict: you fall in love with projects. You are drawn to people who are a little lost, a little unfinished, because you know exactly how to help them grow. Then you spend the relationship being their coach, their landlord of emotional stability, their five-year plan. They grow, sometimes right out of the relationship, and you're left holding the watering can wondering what happened. The other flag is pride. You'd rather be right than close, and you can hold a position long after you've forgotten why you took it. Neither of these makes you a bad partner. They make you a tired one. Look for someone who is already growing on their own. You don't need to be anyone's sunlight. You get to just be the tree next to them.
text.what-you-need: You need a partner with their own roots. Someone who has plans you didn't write, opinions you can't talk them out of, and a life that would keep going if you took a month off from being impressive. You need respect more than you need flattery, and you can tell the difference instantly. You also need someone who notices when you're tired, because you won't say it. The tree doesn't announce that it's thirsty. Practically: you love best with someone who keeps their word, who argues fair, and who lets you lead in some places and takes the lead in others without a power struggle. The love that suits you is less fireworks, more forest. Two tall things growing side by side, close enough to share shade, far enough apart to both get light.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Gap, you love like a promise. Steady, loyal, the person everyone wishes they'd dated first.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Also the person who turns a second date into a five-year development plan.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: That's devotion! You see who someone could become.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: And then you date who they could become instead of who's actually sitting there.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: The right person already has roots. You don't have to grow them.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Put down the watering can, babe. Nobody asked to be your project.

spring.intro: Spring is Wood's own season, so a spring-born Gap Wood arrives in love already at full height. You are the tree in April, growing in every direction at once, and when you fall you fall with a plan. You decide early, you say it plainly, and you expect the other person to keep up. That confidence is gorgeous on a first date and exhausting by month three if nobody pushes back. In-season Wood has plenty of drive and very little give, so your love lesson is pruning, which in saju is Metal's job. A partner with clear edges, who says no and means it, does not shrink you. They give your growth a shape worth looking at.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Spring Gap, you planted a whole orchard on date two. Let them see one tree first.

summer.intro: Summer belongs to Fire, and Wood is what Fire burns, so a summer-born Gap Wood spends itself keeping everyone warm. In love you are the generous one: the planner, the driver, the person who books the table and remembers which seat they like. You give shade and fuel without being asked, and people fall for how safe that feels. The catch is that a tree in July dries out. You pour into a relationship until you notice, quite suddenly, that nobody has watered you in weeks, and then you go silent instead of saying so. Water is your resource element, which in love means being looked after and letting someone else carry the plan for once.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Summer Gap, you give everyone shade. Sit under someone else's tree this time. You've earned it.

autumn.intro: Autumn belongs to Metal, and Metal is the axe that cuts Wood. An autumn-born Gap Wood grows up under pressure, which makes you one of the most disciplined lovers of the ten. You do not fall carelessly. You test, you measure, you check whether this person will still respect you after the first argument. Being shaped by Metal makes you loyal and honest, but it also makes you brace for criticism before any arrives. You can hear a small comment about your plans as a verdict on your worth. The right person for you is not soft or vague. They are direct and warm in the same sentence, so the cut feels like care, not judgement.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Autumn Gap, not every 'are you sure?' is an attack. Sometimes they just want the details.

winter.intro: Winter is Water's season, and Water feeds Wood, so a winter-born Gap Wood has deep roots and a cold canopy. You have plenty of inner support, ideas, memory and patience, but the warmth that makes a tree blossom is in short supply. In love that looks like a slow, sincere start. You might like someone for months while appearing completely neutral. Once you commit, you are steady through anything, the kind of partner who turns up in February with a spare umbrella and no complaints. What you need is Fire: someone who laughs easily, says the affectionate thing out loud, and pulls you into the sun. Your cool exterior is not a lack of feeling. It is just midwinter.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Winter Gap, you've liked them since October. Maybe mention it before the blossoms do.

strength.strong: A strong Gap Wood in love is a tree that never learned to bend. Your chart is full of Wood and Water, so you have conviction, stamina and a very clear sense of how a relationship should go. Partners feel protected by you and sometimes managed by you. Your blind spot is pushing: deciding the pace, the plans, even the timeline for 'I love you', then reading hesitation as disloyalty. The fix is not being smaller. Ask more than you announce. Let your partner own some decisions entirely, and notice how relieved you feel when you are not the only one holding the trunk up.
strength.weak: A weak Gap Wood has the heart of a tall tree and not enough soil to match. With little Wood or Water in your chart, you still want to lead and protect in love, but you overextend to prove you can. You say yes to plans that wear you out, carry the emotional load, and feel guilty asking for help. Your blind spot is shrinking quietly while looking strong. You may stay in something uneven because leaving feels like failing. Choose partners who are generous with encouragement. Let someone hold the umbrella sometimes. Being supported does not make you less of a tree.

balance_text.too_much_wood: Too much Wood in your chart turns love into a growth plan. You want things to move forward, define the relationship, make progress, and slow phases make you restless. You can also be stubborn in arguments, holding your position like a tree in wind. In love this looks like big intentions and a little impatience. Balance it with Metal energy: clear agreements, pruning what isn't working, and accepting that some things are already finished growing. Not every relationship needs to become a forest. Some are perfect as a single, steady tree.
balance_text.missing_wood: Missing Wood means beginnings are your hard part. You might wait for the other person to make the first move, define things, or suggest the next step, and you can stay in a comfortable but stuck situation for too long. Your love is real, it just doesn't push. Balance it by practising small starts: suggest the date, send the first text, say what you hope for out loud. Green things help as reminders, a plant by your bed, a green phone case. Love grows when someone plants it. Sometimes that someone is you.
balance_text.too_much_fire: Too much Fire makes your love bright, fast and a little combustible. You fall hard, flirt boldly and feel everything at full volume. The highs are glorious. The lows, when attention drops, feel like the lights went out. You can also lose interest once the excitement settles. Balance it with Water energy: slowing down, letting quiet evenings count, and sitting with feelings before reacting. Ask yourself if you love the person or the thrill. The best flame for you burns steady, not just bright.
balance_text.missing_fire: Missing Fire means passion and visibility don't come easily in love. You might care deeply but struggle to show it, hold back affection until you're sure, or feel awkward with romantic gestures. People can mistake your reserve for disinterest. Balance it by letting warmth out in small, brave doses: a compliment, a hug that lasts a second longer, a little playfulness. Warm colours and sunlight help you feel more expressive. You don't need fireworks. You just need people to see that the light is on.
balance_text.too_much_earth: Too much Earth makes you a steady, devoted partner who can get a little stuck. You value security, routine and loyalty, and you might stay in familiar patterns even when they've stopped making you happy. Change feels risky. You may also over-care, taking on your partner's problems as your own. Balance it with Wood energy: try something new together, plan an adventure, let the relationship grow in surprising directions. Safe is wonderful. Safe and alive is even better.
balance_text.missing_earth: Missing Earth means love can feel unsteady. You might worry about where things stand, struggle to settle into commitment, or jump between highs and lows. You can also find it hard to trust that someone will stay. Balance it by building small, reliable rituals: a weekly date, a regular call, a shared routine. Choose partners who are consistent rather than exciting. Earth tones and home-cooked meals help you feel grounded. Stability isn't boring. For you, it's what lets love feel safe enough to enjoy.
balance_text.too_much_metal: Too much Metal gives you strong standards and very clear boundaries in love. You know what you want and what you won't tolerate, which is healthy, until it becomes rigid. You can be critical, quick to judge, or end things abruptly when disappointed. Balance it with Fire energy: warmth, forgiveness, play. Let small mistakes be small. Say the kind thing before the honest thing. Strong boundaries keep you safe. Soft edges let people actually come close enough to love you.
balance_text.missing_metal: Missing Metal means boundaries are your hard part in love. You might say yes when you mean no, stay too long, or let people treat you less well than you deserve because you don't want conflict. Your heart is open, sometimes too open. Balance it by practising clear, simple limits: "I'm not okay with that," without a long explanation. Decluttering and white or silver accents can help you feel sharper. Boundaries aren't walls. They're the frame that makes the picture of your love clear.
balance_text.too_much_water: Too much Water makes your love deep, intuitive and sometimes overwhelming. You feel everything, read every mood and can get lost in emotional currents or imagined stories. You may also avoid commitment, drifting rather than choosing. Balance it with Earth energy: grounding conversations, practical plans, partners who are steady and clear. Write down what actually happened before reacting to what you feel happened. Your depth is beautiful. It just needs a shore so you don't get swept away.
balance_text.missing_water: Missing Water means emotional depth and rest don't come easily in love. You might stay busy, keep conversations practical, or struggle to sit with vulnerable feelings, yours or your partner's. Love can feel like a to-do list. Balance it with slow, quiet moments: late talks, journaling, listening without fixing. Navy and black, water by your bed, and slow evenings help you soften. You don't need to drown in feelings. Just let yourself wade in a little deeper.

too_much_wood.speaker: yeon
too_much_wood.text: Too much Wood: you want it defined, labelled and growing by Thursday. Breathe.

too_much_wood.speaker: bom
too_much_wood.text: Your hope is beautiful. Let it grow at the speed of a real person.

too_much_fire.speaker: yeon
too_much_fire.text: Too much Fire: you fall hard, fast and loudly. Then the second act bores you.

too_much_fire.speaker: bom
too_much_fire.text: Your passion is a gift. Let it simmer a while. Slow love tastes better.

too_much_earth.speaker: yeon
too_much_earth.text: Too much Earth: staying somewhere stale because leaving takes effort isn't loyalty. It's inertia.

too_much_earth.speaker: bom
too_much_earth.text: Your loyalty is rare. Make sure it's going somewhere that still feeds you.

too_much_metal.speaker: yeon
too_much_metal.text: Too much Metal: your dating checklist has forty points. Nobody passes. Including you.

too_much_metal.speaker: bom
too_much_metal.text: Standards protect you. Leave one door open for someone surprising.

too_much_water.speaker: yeon
too_much_water.text: Too much Water: you wrote a whole love story in your head. They've read none of it.

too_much_water.speaker: bom
too_much_water.text: Your depth is gorgeous. Share a little of it with the real person.

missing_wood.speaker: bom
missing_wood.text: Missing Wood? Love won't start itself. Send the first text. Plant something.

missing_wood.speaker: yeon
missing_wood.text: Waiting for them to make the move isn't patience. It's hiding behind a nice word.

missing_fire.speaker: bom
missing_fire.text: Missing Fire? Your love is real, it just whispers. Let someone hear it.

missing_fire.speaker: yeon
missing_fire.text: A compliment you only think doesn't count. Say it, then survive the blushing.

missing_earth.speaker: bom
missing_earth.text: Missing Earth? You love brightly but drift. A small weekly ritual keeps you anchored.

missing_earth.speaker: yeon
missing_earth.text: Three crushes, zero follow-through. Pick one and show up twice in a row.

missing_metal.speaker: bom
missing_metal.text: Missing Metal? Your kindness needs a boundary. A no keeps your yes worth something.

missing_metal.speaker: yeon
missing_metal.text: Three cancellations and a fourth chance isn't generosity. It's a pattern you're funding.

missing_water.speaker: bom
missing_water.text: Missing Water? You act before you feel. Pause and ask what you actually want.

missing_water.speaker: yeon
missing_water.text: Over someone in a weekend isn't healing. It's skipping the chapter. Read it.
